title: lint_migration_schema.py reports false-positive BLOCKER on public.<table> mentioned inside a -- prose comment (081_iss101_timers_failed_status.sql)
notes: Discovered incidentally while validating the ISS-0108 fix (GitHub #368). Running `python tools/lint_migration_schema.py migrations` on unmodified main fails with a BLOCKER on line 13 of 081_iss101_timers_failed_status.sql, which is a plain -- prose comment mentioning 'public.timers' in passing ('public.timers was dropped by GBL-073'), not executable SQL. The linter's _BUSINESS_TABLE_PATTERN regex scans raw line text including -- comments, so it flags the comment even though the file's actual DDL is already correctly unqualified per TNT-02 convention.
root_cause: lint_file() in tools/lint_migration_schema.py has no exclusion for plain `--`-prefixed line comments outside of DO $$ blocks; it only has special handling for string literals inside DO blocks (a deliberate, separate check for embedded dynamic SQL). Ordinary trailing/standalone `--` comments are scanned as if they were SQL.
candidate_resolution: Strip `--`-comment suffixes from each line before running _BUSINESS_TABLE_PATTERN/_PERMITTED_TABLE_PATTERN matching, leaving the existing DO-block string-literal scan untouched.
resolution: Implemented in tools/lint_migration_schema.py: added _strip_line_comment() which strips a trailing `--` line comment from each line, honoring single-quoted string literals (a `--` inside a string does not end the code portion). lint_file() now runs _BUSINESS_TABLE_PATTERN/_PERMITTED_TABLE_PATTERN and the DO-block boundary detector against the comment-stripped text instead of the raw line, so prose that merely mentions a business table name (e.g. `-- ... public.timers was dropped ...`) no longer trips a false BLOCKER. Verified with synthetic cases: comment-only mention (now clean), real `public.timers` SQL reference (still BLOCKER), code-with-trailing-comment (code portion still checked, comment ignored), and a `--` embedded inside a single-quoted string literal in a DO block (still correctly flagged, not mistaken for a comment start). Full `python tools/lint_migration_schema.py migrations` run: 97 files scanned, exit 0, same MINOR count as before (no regression).
files_to_change_note: Also fixed the immediate false-positive by rewording the comment in migrations/081_iss101_timers_failed_status.sql (in the ISS-0108 change) so lint_migration_schema.py migrations exits 0 today; the linter itself still has the underlying gap and should be hardened as this issue's primary fix so future comments mentioning business tables don't trip the same false positive.
prevention: When writing comments in migration files, avoid the exact substring `public.<business_table>` where possible until this linter gap is closed.
Prefer stripping comments before applying content-based lint regexes in any future SQL/text linting tool in this repo.
